title: Node preflight and Helm postinstall trace
content:
Context:
- Hit intermittent failures on new node pools: nodes come up but are NotReady or kubelet restarts repeatedly after boot. Helm releases that run post-install hooks fail because jobs stay Pending (no node match / scheduling backoff). Trying to capture breadcrumbs for repro & next steps.

Symptoms observed (latest incident 2024-11-02):
- Node enters cluster (kubectl get nodes shows Ready briefly) then goes NotReady after ~30-60s.
- kubelet systemd unit restarts (~systemd: start request repeated too quickly for kubelet.service).
- Helm chart post-install Job pods stuck Pending; kubectl describe pod shows "0/3 nodes are available: 3 node(s) didn't match node selector" in some cases, and in others pods never schedule because kubelet hasn't registered all node labels/taints.
- cloud-init log shows mount failures for ephemeral device (/dev/nvme0n1) on ~15% of boots.

Commands I ran (copy/paste from session):
- kubectl get nodes -o wide --show-labels
- kubectl describe node ip-10-0-8-42.us-west-2.compute.internal
- sudo journalctl -u kubelet -b --no-pager | sed -n '1,200p'
- sudo journalctl -k | grep -i nvme
- sudo cat /var/log/cloud-init-output.log | sed -n '1,400p'
- lsblk -o NAME,SIZE,TYPE,MOUNTPOINT,MODEL; df -hT | egrep -i 'ephemeral|nvme|/mnt'
- sudo systemctl status cloud-init-local.service cloud-init.service kubelet.service --no-pager
- sudo crictl ps -a; sudo crictl logs <helm-hook-pod-container-id>
- kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide | egrep 'cni|kube-proxy|kubelet'

Key error snippets saved:
- kubelet journal: "failed to register node: nodes \"ip-10-0-8-42\" not found (might be timing race)"
- kubelet crashloop: "runtime/cgo: pthread_create failed: Resource temporarily unavailable" (suspicious, need to correlate with memory/cgroup limits)
- cloud-init: "mount: /mnt/ephemeral: unknown filesystem type 'xfs'" and "cloud-init[1234]: Device /dev/nvme0n1 not found"
- systemd: "Dependency failed for Kubelet Container Runtime Interface" when containerd socket never appears due to device mount ordering

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) boot ordering race: cloud-init that formats/mounts ephemeral disks sometimes fails or is delayed -> container runtime (containerd) cannot create required state dirs -> kubelet fails -> node never reaches stable Ready state. This explains intermittent nature.
2) instance type with NVMe presents device name jitter (/dev/nvme0n1 vs /dev/nvme1n1) depending on timing -> cloud-init mounts wrong device -> mount fails.
3) Kernel memory pressure or ulimit limits cause pthread_create failures in containerd/libprocess -> service restart loops. Correlate with dmesg OOMs.
4) Helm post-install jobs expect node labels/taints applied by bootstrap script; if kubelet restarts before node-label agent runs, jobs remain pending.

Repro steps I ran or plan to run:
- repro on staging pool: create 3 nodes with same user-data, watch cloud-init logs via serial console (gcloud/aws console) to capture device enumeration order.
- add pause between ephemeral formatting and starting containerd (simulate failure) to see if kubelet regresses.
- boot with kernel cmdline flag to log early printk to catch device enumeration.
- temporarily add an ExecStartPre on kubelet.service to check for /var/lib/containerd existence and block until mounted (as a bandaid).

Short-term mitigations attempted:
- cordon and drain affected node, recreated nodepool with retry count and increased cloud-init retries (setcloudcfg: retries=10). Observed drop in incidence but not eliminated.
- added a Systemd 'After=cloud-final.service' on containerd unit in staging to force ordering (risky in prod).
- adjusted Helm chart job tolerations to allow scheduling on control plane nodes for critical post-install hooks (temporary workaround).

Observed differences across AMIs / images:
- AMI A (old): consistent mount naming, nearly zero failures during 100 boots.
- AMI B (newer kernel): ~12% boots fail with nvme enumeration error.
- AMI C (custom): containerd version mismatch causing "timeout waiting for container runtime" in kubelet.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Capture dmesg and cloud-init serial console output for one failed instance (I couldn't get serial console logs for the first failure). Need cloud admin helper.
- Validate if cloud provider changed NVMe device naming semantics in the newer image/kernel. File infra ticket to request kernel changelog / mapping.
- Run mem/cgroup stress test after boot to see if pthread_create errors are reproducible (could be a containerd memory leak).
- Add more telemetry: kubelet start time, containerd start time, cloud-init completion timestamp to node metadata (might require custom datasource scripting).
- Follow up in RDW-1873 with infra team; link above includes the small systemd change I tried.

Notes on debugging commands to share with on-call peer:
- quick triage: ssh node -> sudo journalctl -u kubelet -b -n 200; sudo journalctl -u containerd -b -n 200; sudo cat /var/log/cloud-init-output.log | tail -n 200; lsblk; sudo blkid; df -hT; sudo systemctl list-dependencies --reverse kubelet | sed -n '1,200p'
- if cloud-init shows missing device, check /dev/disk/by-id and cloud-init data source for mapping.
- inspect kubelet config: cat /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml for node labels that Helm jobs depend on.

Final thoughts / next actions (short):
- Get serial console dump for one failure (ask infra) and attach to RDW-1873.
- Reproduce with controlled sleep in cloud-init to trigger race and capture timestamps. Add a minimal systemd unit to log device detection order.
- If repro confirmed, propose change: make containerd (and kubelet) wait for ephemeral mount or add an idempotent mount-check script invoked via ExecStartPre.

Odd/interesting observations for later:
- In one failure, kubelet reported NodeReady then immediately advertised kubelet.labels: alpha.server.alpha/nodepool=legacy which was missing in later boots; suggests the labeling agent runs after kubelet start in some images.
- Two nodes that failed initially came up healthy after a reboot (so transient).

If anyone else picks this up: tag me (Priya) and paste cloud-init output + journalctl of first 10 minutes post boot. Prefer serial console logs over SSH for early-boot races.

-- end of scratchpad --
